headline: Work is trading your time and effort for value—contributing something others find worthwhile
universal_truth: Time is finite; how you spend it working shapes what you build and who you become
fun_facts: The average person spends about 90,000 hours at work over a lifetime
Work provides more than money—it gives structure, purpose, social connection, and identity
The nature of work is constantly changing—today's jobs didn't exist decades ago
discussion_questions: What do you trade your time for?
Does your work feel like fair exchange?
What would meaningful work look like for you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You have 24 hours each day. Much of it goes to work—trading time and effort for compensation. But work is more than just money. It's what you contribute, how you spend your life, who you become through doing.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Work takes most of your waking hours. Why does it matter beyond paying bills?

options.text: Work provides multiple returns—money yes, but also structure, purpose, identity, and contribution; what you do with your hours shapes who you are; work is how you participate in society's productive life
options.response: Yes. Work isn't just income. It's where you develop skills, find purpose, belong to something larger. Bad work drains you. Good work energizes. What you do with your hours matters.

options.text: Work is just how you pay bills
options.response: Bills must be paid, but work also provides meaning, structure, growth—or can drain all three...

q1.title: Fair Exchange
q1.script: Is your work fairly compensated? Do you give more than you receive? The exchange should be mutual—your contribution matched by what you get back. Unfair work depletes.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Fair Exchange"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Meaningful vs Empty
q2.script: Not all work is equal. Work that uses your strengths, contributes to something worthwhile, and develops you differs from work that just fills hours. Seek meaning where possible.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Beyond Employment
q3.script: Work isn't just paid jobs. Caring for family, volunteering, creating—these are work too. All labor has value, whether or not it's compensated. Value your unpaid contributions.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Time is finite. How you spend it working shapes what you build and who you become. Trade your time wisely.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 340! Tomorrow, we'll explore keeping for later—saving. Until then, consider whether your work is fair exchange.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Work Audit - Is the Trade Fair?
growTrack.activity: Consider your work—paid and unpaid. What do you give? What do you receive? Is the exchange fair? Does your work provide meaning beyond money? What would better work look like?
